STILL OPEN, the whole relic-identity half: (G1) sts2_rl/relics/calling_bell.py:22 still hard-codes `RELICS = ('anchor', 'gremlin_horn', 'mummified_hand')`, i.e. CallingBell.GenerateRewards' TestMode.IsOn arm (CallingBell.cs:39-52), where the shipping arm (CallingBell.cs:53-63) builds `new RelicReward(RelicRarity.Common, Owner)`, `(Uncommon, ...)` and `(Rare, ...)`, each resolved in RelicReward.Populate by `RelicFactory.PullNextRelicFromFront(Player, rarity)` (RelicReward.cs:75-96) — so every run that takes the Bell gets the same three fixed relics instead of one random Common, one Uncommon and one Rare. Note for whoever fixes G2: the pinned-rarity overload does NOT roll rarity (RelicFactory.cs:31-33 calls PullNextRelicFromFront(player, rarity, _ => true) with no RollRarity), so the remaining cost is the three bag consumptions, not three PlayerRng.Rewards draws — the original G2 text overstated the stream cost. Rule 7: sts2_rl/run.py, sts2_rl/driver.py, src/Core/Rewards/RelicReward.cs and src/Core/Factories/RelicFactory.cs are not hashed here. The fixed Anchor / Gremlin Horn / Mummified Hand list (CallingBell.cs:39-52) is gone. EXECUTED 2026-07-29 on three seeds: the grab bag goes 96 -> 93 (G2's recorded number was 96 -> 96) and the relics granted are seed-dependent -- ['blood_vial', 'parrying_shield', 'game_piece'], ['bag_of_marbles', 'bowler_hat', 'pocketwatch'], ['strawberry', 'miniature_cannon', 'unceasing_top'] -- where G1's recorded number was the same three fixed relics on every seed. So the wrong relics are no longer granted AND the three pulls are consumed, which are exactly the two observables the entries were split to keep separate. The text it replaced read: MECHANISM: CallingBell.cs:34-64 has two arms. The `if (TestMode.IsOn)` arm (lines 39-52) builds three RelicRewards with FIXED models -- Anchor, Gremlin Horn, Mummified Hand. The shipping arm (53-63) builds `new RelicReward(RelicRarity.Common, Owner)`, `(RelicRarity.Uncommon, ...)` and `(RelicRarity.Rare, ...)`, each of which resolves its relic in RelicReward.Populate via `RelicFactory.PullNextRelicFromFront(Player, rarity)` (RelicReward.cs:75-96). calling_bell.py:21 hard-codes `RELICS = ('anchor', 'gremlin_horn', 'mummified_hand')` -- the test arm. TestMode.IsOn is a unit-test flag: `TestMode.TurnOnInternal` (TestMode.cs:38) is documented 'NEVER CALL THIS. Only calls should be in NetCoreRunner and CiCoreRunner' and has no caller anywhere under src/, so the shipping game always takes the second arm. REACHABILITY (LIVE, executed -- `py audit/tools/relic_probes.py batch3`): `run.add_relic('calling_bell')` yields relics ['calling_bell', 'anchor', 'gremlin_horn', 'mummified_hand'] on every seed, where the game yields one random Common, one Uncommon and one Rare from the run's grab bag. Both sides ported: Calling Bell is granted by the ported Darv shrine (events/darv.py) and the sim has a working rarity pull (`RunState.pull_relic_from_front`, run.py:559-566, used by the elite-relic reward path). This is not a dormancy question at all -- the wrong relics are granted in every run that takes the Bell.

guards.what: G4: `Hook.ShouldAddToDeck` is consulted by CardPileCmd.Add (CardPileCmd.cs:384) on the curse; the sim has no such hook
guards.rationale: VOCABULARY RULING (2026-07-26 relic fix pass), applied at every dead-in-the-source site in this tier so it stops contradicting itself. When a C# member the sim omits is DEAD IN THE GAME SOURCE ITSELF -- zero overrides, zero producers, zero callers anywhere under src/ -- the correct verdict is `faithful`, not `waiver`. PROMPT.md v6 item 3, which the relic stream itself wrote, settles the principle for the mirror-image case: 'a waiver is in-scope-adjacent and declined, and here there is no source behaviour to be faithful to.' A waiver claims something in scope was deliberately not audited; here there is nothing to decline, because the member provably cannot fire in any run of the shipping game and cannot become live by porting more content -- it would take a change to the game's own source. `faithful` also states the stronger and more useful fact: the two codebases have the SAME observable. Before this pass the relic tier split 8 waivers against 5 faithfuls on identical reasoning; these entries are now all `faithful` (binding rule 3). NOTE: this ruling does NOT touch MULTIPLAYER gates (`player != base.Owner`, `Players.Count == 1`), which stay `waiver` -- the shared contract names multiplayer as out of scope outright, and unlike a dead member a player count really can differ in the shipping game; the sim simply does not model that mode. AT THIS SITE: The finding is unchanged and still executed: `grep -rn should_add_to_deck sts2_rl/ --include=*.py` returns ZERO hits, and on the C# side `grep -rn ShouldAddToDeck src/` returns exactly four lines -- the dispatch at CardPileCmd.cs:384, the Hook wrapper at Hook.cs:2084-2088 and the `public virtual` base declaration at AbstractModel.cs:2144. Not one override exists in the whole game, so the hook is dead code in C# too, not unported content. ONLY THE VERDICT CHANGES. Rule 7: CardPileCmd.cs, Hook.cs and AbstractModel.cs are not hashed here.

AddCurseToDeck asserts the card is a Curse, creates it on the run, and routes it through `Add(card, PileType.Deck)` (CardPileCmd.cs:1037-1056). run.add_card (run.py:524-537, was :341-354) runs modify_card_being_added_to_deck before the append and after_card_added_to_deck after it, which are the two deck-add hooks the sim models. The curse is ported and correct: cards/curse_of_the_bell.py is CardType.CURSE, eternal=True, max_upgrade_level 0. EXECUTED: the probe reports `curse added: ['curse_of_the_bell']`.

guards.what: N2: the ORDER -- curse first, relics second
guards.rationale: CallingBell.cs:29-31 adds the curse, waits, then offers; calling_bell.py:26-28 adds the curse then the relics. Recorded because it is load-bearing for any granted relic that reacts to the deck: Mummified Hand and Gremlin Horn do not, but a fixed G1 pulling a random Common could pull one that does (e.g. a deck-size reader), and the curse must already be in the deck when it lands.
